newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said Commission President Jacques Santer and Commissioners Emma Bonino and Franz Fischler would hold a news conference at 1530/1430 GMT, following the European Parliament's vote on a censure motion against the European Commission for its handling of the BSE crisis.
Vale de Almeida also announced a technical briefing by Eurostat officials on budgetary measures after the Commission's midday briefing.
Vale de Almeida said President Santer had sent a telegram to the Chinese autorities following the annoucement of former Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's death.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said World Trade Organisation Director General Renato Ruggiero had chosen the three panelist to look into the dispute over the Helms-Burton law. He said those panelists were Arthur Dunkel of Switzerland, Ted Woodfield of New Zealand and Tommy Koh of Singapore.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on the judgments delivered by the Court of Justice.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/137: Joint EU/South Africa press statement on bilaterla negotiations.
- IP/97/138: Financial services: Commissioner Monti welcomers adoption of investor compensation directive.
- IP/97/141: The contribution of European research to the treatment of leukemia.
- IP/97/142: The Commission authorises the acquisition by the Sidmar group of control of Ferrometalli Safem S.p.A.
- Eurostat news release No 15/97: EU GDP up by 0.81%.
